     9	
    10	Implement configurable model settings for the persona system, replacing hardcoded YAML-only model configuration with a GUI-managed model registry and per-persona model assignment system. Users will be able to register available models, assign them to individual personas across all three suites (ledger, standalone, ledger-support), and set a default model — all through the existing GUI's Configuration screen, restructured with tabs. Each model registry entry includes a `cc_model` field (the Claude Code model setting, defaulting to `"inherit"`), allowing per-persona Claude Code model configuration alongside the VS Code / orchestrator model. A built-in "Inherit / Auto" model option (slug `inherit`) lets users defer model selection entirely: VS Code omits the `model` frontmatter field (using whatever model the user has selected in the model picker), Claude Code gets `model: 'inherit'` (deferring to the user's configured model), and the orchestrator skips the override (falling back to YAML-based resolution).     11	
    12	## Architectural Context
    13	
    14	The system currently resolves model slugs through a two-layer YAML mechanism:
    15	
    16	1. **Suite-wide default:** `personas/ledger/src/meta/_shared.yaml` → `default_model` / `default_model_slug` (currently `Claude Sonnet 4.6`)
    17	2. **Per-persona override:** Individual YAML files (e.g., `1-planner.yaml`) optionally set `model` / `model_slug` (currently only Planner and PM override to `Claude Opus 4.6`)
    18	
    19	The persona build system (`personas/plugins/ledger/index.js`) resolves model values at build time via fallback logic and injects them into templates (VS Code frontmatter gets `model: '{{model}}'`). The orchestrator (`orchestrator/src/utils/persona_models.py`) independently reads the same YAML files at startup to populate `Config.stage_models`.
    20	
    21	The GUI runs as an HTTP server from `mcp-server/gui/`, with settings stored at `{ledgerRoot}/gui-config.json`. The server has access to `WORKSPACE_ROOT` (derived from `mcp-server/..` in `mcp-server/src/utils/ledger-root.ts`), which enables it to locate files in the `personas/` directory.
    22	
    23	The `name-mapping.json` file is auto-generated by `scripts/build-personas.js` on every build but currently omits model fields from its entries.
    24	
    25	## Approach / Architecture
    26	
    27	Introduce a file-based model registry and assignment system at `personas/model-registry/` with three files:
    28	
    29	- **`default.json`** — shipped default models (tracked in Git)
    30	- **`local.json`** — user-registered models (gitignored, auto-created on first use)
    31	- **`assignments.json`** — per-persona model assignments + default model selection (gitignored, auto-created on first use)
    32	
    33	The GUI Configuration screen is restructured with a tab system (General, Persona Models, Model Registry). New API endpoints provide bulk save for the model registry and CRUD for assignments. Both the persona build system (all three suite plugins — ledger, standalone, ledger-support) and the orchestrator are updated to read `assignments.json` as the highest-priority override layer in the model resolution chain:
    34	
    35	```
    36	assignments.json (user GUI config) > per-persona YAML > _shared.yaml default
    37	```
    38	
    39	The `name-mapping.json` generation is extended to include `model` and `model_slug` fields, reflecting the resolved model for each persona after the full priority chain is applied.
    40	
    41	## Rationale
    42	
    43	- **Separate files for registry vs. assignments** — different lifecycles: registry is "what's available", assignments is "what's chosen". Both are gitignored (except shipped defaults) because model preferences are per-developer.
    44	- **`default.json` is a seed, not a runtime layer** — shipped defaults are copied into `local.json` on first access (auto-initialization) or via the "Load Defaults" button. Once copied, entries are fully editable and deletable like any user-registered model. There is no concept of "built-in" vs "custom" at runtime — `local.json` is the single source of truth for the model list. `default.json` exists solely so new installations start with a sensible set of models and so future releases can introduce new defaults via "Load Defaults".
    45	- **Files in `personas/model-registry/`** — colocated with the persona source they configure. Both the build system and orchestrator already operate relative to the workspace root and can locate this directory. The GUI accesses it via the existing `WORKSPACE_ROOT` constant.
    46	- **Priority chain preserves YAML as fallback** — users who never touch the GUI get the same behavior as today. The GUI is purely additive.
    47	- **All persona suites supported** — model assignments use persona `id` from `name-mapping.json` (e.g., `ledger-1-planner`, `developer-standalone`, `standalone-ledger-bootstrapper`) as keys, covering all three suites. This ensures every persona in the system can have a model override, not just the 9 ledger personas.
    48	- **UUID values in assignments, resolved at consumption** — `assignments.json` stores model UUIDs as values rather than slugs. UUIDs are stable across slug renames, eliminating the class of sync bugs that arise when slugs are changed out-of-band (bypassing any cascade). Both the build system and orchestrator read `assignments.json` alongside `local.json`, build a UUID-to-slug map, and resolve locally before applying the priority chain. The `getResolvedAssignments()` function in `model-registry.ts` provides the same resolution for API consumers. The frontend works with UUIDs directly and resolves them to model names client-side using the already-loaded model registry.
    49	- **Bulk save, not instant CRUD** — the Model Registry tab and Persona Models tab both use a local-state-then-save pattern: edits accumulate in the frontend, dirty indicators show what changed, and a single Save button commits everything. This avoids partial-state problems (e.g., a failed mid-edit API call leaving the registry inconsistent) and gives users a clear undo path (just don't save).
    50	- **Tab system follows knowledge.js pattern** — the only existing tab implementation in the GUI; reusing the same pattern maintains visual consistency and avoids introducing a new abstraction for a single use.
    51	
    52	## Considered Alternatives
    53	
    54	| Decision | Chosen Shape | Alternatives Considered | Trade-Off Summary |
    55	|----------|--------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
    56	| Assignment storage location | `personas/model-registry/assignments.json` | (a) Extend `gui-config.json` (b) Store in `{ledgerRoot}/model-assignments.json` (c) Write to `name-mapping.json` | (a) mixes GUI settings with persona config, making cross-system consumption harder; (b) forces build system/orchestrator to know the ledger root, which they currently don't; (c) `name-mapping.json` is auto-regenerated, so user edits would be lost |
    57	| Model registry scope | Workspace-level (`personas/model-registry/`) | Per-user global (`~/.ai-insights/models.json`) | Workspace-level keeps models colocated with personas and avoids a new global config path; different workspaces can have different model sets |
    58	| GUI tab approach | Hand-coded tabs matching knowledge.js pattern | Generic reusable `UI.tabs()` component | Only two views need tabs; extracting a generic component is speculative without a third consumer |
    59	| Model registry architecture | `default.json` (seed) + `local.json` (working copy, auto-initialized) | (a) Runtime merge of default + local (b) Single merged file | Seed + working copy is simpler: reads always go to `local.json`, no merge logic on every API call. `default.json` is only consulted during auto-initialization and "Load Defaults". (a) adds complexity to every read path; (b) makes diffing against shipped defaults harder |
    60	| "Inherit / Auto" representation | Reserved `inherit` slug in the default registry, handled as sentinel by consumers | (a) Boolean flag on each assignment `{ slug, inherit: true }` (b) Separate "no model" dropdown option with no registry entry | A registry entry is the simplest shape — assignments store the sentinel UUID like any other model; after resolution via `getResolvedAssignments()`, consumers check `slug === 'inherit'` on the resolved slug — no special-case structure || Model entry primary key | UUID `id` field, auto-generated on creation | (a) Slug as primary key (b) Auto-incrementing numeric ID | Slug-as-PK couples identity to a mutable field — renaming a slug would break all API references and require URL changes. UUID is globally unique, stable across renames, and since assignments store UUIDs, slug changes never require cascading into assignments. Numeric IDs risk collision on merge of default + local registries. |
    61	| Assignment key format (values) | UUIDs in `assignments.json`, resolved to slugs by consumers | Slugs stored directly | UUIDs are stable across slug renames, eliminating the sync risk of out-of-band edits bypassing a cascade. The coupling concern (UUID → slug resolution) is mitigated by a single utility: `getResolvedAssignments()` in `model-registry.ts` for API consumers; read-both-files-and-resolve locally for the build system and orchestrator. Consumers receive the same slug-based shape they already expect. |
    62	| Assignment key format (keys) | Persona `id` from `name-mapping.json` (e.g., `ledger-1-planner`) | Workflow manifest role IDs | Persona `id` covers all three suites (ledger, standalone, ledger-support); workflow manifest role IDs only cover the 9 ledger roles. Since model assignment applies to all personas, the key space must include all suites. |
    63	| Persona model display UX | Click-to-edit with resolved model as static text + edit icon + dirty indicator | (a) Always-visible dropdowns (b) Modal edit form | Static display reduces visual noise on a page with 20+ personas across 3 suites. The edit icon is a familiar pattern. Dirty indicators give clear feedback before saving. Always-visible dropdowns would dominate the page and obscure the current state. |
    64	| Model registry save UX | Bulk save (local state + single Save button) | Per-model instant CRUD (individual POST/PUT/DELETE) | Bulk save enables dirty indicators, prevents partial-state errors, and gives users a clear discard path (navigate away without saving). Instant CRUD requires immediate error handling per operation and has no concept of "unsaved changes". |
    65	## Pattern Alignment
    66	
    67	- **GUI handler pattern** — follows `api-repos.ts` pattern: pure async functions, Zod validation, `ApiError` throws — `mcp-server/gui/api-repos.ts`
    68	- **Config module pattern** — follows `config.ts` singleton cache + atomic writes + file watcher — `mcp-server/src/gui/config.ts`
    69	- **Tab CSS pattern** — follows `.knowledge-tabs` / `.knowledge-tab` styling — `mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css` L2867–2902
    70	- **API client pattern** — follows `request(method, path, body)` thin wrapper — `mcp-server/gui/public/api-client.js`
    71	- **Orchestrator model resolution** — extends existing `extract_persona_model_slugs()` rather than replacing it — `orchestrator/src/utils/persona_models.py`
    72	- **Departure: generic tab CSS class names** — uses `.config-tabs` / `.config-tab` instead of `.knowledge-tabs` to avoid coupling tab styling to a specific view. The CSS rules are identical; only the class prefix changes.
    73	
    74	## Detailed Steps
    75	
    76	### 1. Create model registry default file
    77	
    78	Create `personas/model-registry/default.json` with the shipped default models. Each entry includes a `cc_model` field for the Claude Code model setting (rendered into Claude Code frontmatter as `model: '{{cc_model}}'`). Anthropic models use `"inherit"` (defer to user's Claude Code config), while non-Anthropic models specify the model name explicitly since Claude Code cannot inherit a non-Anthropic model:
    79	
    80	```json
    81	[
    82	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "name": "Inherit / Auto", "slug": "inherit", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    83	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001", "name": "Claude Opus 4.6", "slug": "claude-opus-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    84	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002", "name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6", "slug": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    85	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003", "name": "Gemini 3.5 Flash", "slug": "gemini-3-5-flash", "cc_model": "gemini-3-5-flash" }
    86	]
    87	```
    88	
    89	Default entries use deterministic zero-namespace UUIDs so they are stable across installations and can be referenced reliably by `loadDefaults()` merge logic (match by `id`, not by slug).
    90	
    91	The `inherit` entry is a sentinel: when assigned to a persona, the build system omits the `model` field from VS Code frontmatter (so the user's model picker selection is used), sets `model: 'inherit'` in Claude Code frontmatter, and the orchestrator skips the assignment (falling back to YAML-based resolution).
    92	
    93	### 2. Update `.gitignore`
    94	
    95	Add entries for the user-local model registry files:
    96	
    97	```
    98	/personas/model-registry/local.json
    99	/personas/model-registry/assignments.json
   100	```
